body.target_estimand: \(\theta_g(\mathcal M)=\mathbb E_{\nu}[g(f^U)]\), equivalently \(\mathbb E_{\mu}[g(f)]\) on the canonical carrier

sampling_model.design: Identification is conditional on an exactly supplied observational law \(p\); an optional statistical layer consists of independent draws from \(p\) after the query, order, and alphabets are fixed.
sampling_model.units: Each observational unit reveals one factual vector \(V\in\mathcal X\); the shared exogenous response type is latent.
sampling_model.treatment: Interventions occur only inside the counterfactual query and are not randomized observations in the maintained identification problem.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed because the target is partially identified from the full observational law; known zero-mass cells receive no exogenous atom.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated in the theorem-level kernel. If \(p\) is replaced by empirical frequencies, the compiled cell labels are fixed and the endpoints are sample means, but this standard corollary is outside the novelty claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The lifted linear program gives the order-only optimum, and an attaining structural causal model exists.
The \(\mathrm{SAT}^{\mathrm{lin}}_{\mathrm{counterfact}}\) problem uses inequalities over probability terms on one common domain, and Theorem~11 is fixed-parameter tractable in \(d+n\).
Input-signature satisfiability for recursive finite causal models is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-complete.
Compilation languages are ranked by succinctness and by supported polynomial-time queries and transformations.
Finite canonical structural causal models reduce arbitrary discrete counterfactual bounds to sharp polynomial programs.
Fixed structural equations are compiled into arithmetic circuits to accelerate approximate causal-EM inner-bound computation.

body.tldr: For standard finite order-compatible recursive structural causal models with arbitrary predecessor parent subsets and shared exogenous variation, the sourced causal-order canonicalization permits sharp-bound optimization over a saturated all-predecessor response carrier. A deterministic value-preserving normalizer derives predecessor-only retained contexts from explicit unnested intervention atoms, and the equality partition of their complete prefixes is an exact continuation state. It is also worst-case residual-minimal: a self-contained binary selector construction realizes and pairwise separates all \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) partitions while keeping the factual zero cell outside the retained context set. Representative transitions yield exact conjunction and joint-score compilers whose exponential factors depend on the normalized number of worlds and score terms but not on alphabet cardinalities. Sparse traceback and one exogenous atom per positive observational cell attain the sharp cell-sum endpoints.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact order-only method proves canonical equivalence between parent-subset recursive models and complete all-predecessor response carriers, then enumerates completed response signatures before quotienting them by observational and query evaluations, leaving an alphabet-product optimization space. It does not establish either a value-preserving predecessor normal form for a prefix compiler, complete-prefix equality as an exact local continuation state, or worst-case residual minimality of that state.
project_justification.niche: Explicit unnested queries with few normalized intervention contexts but many endogenous coordinates or large alphabets admit a smaller semantic state on the equivalent canonical carrier: later unrestricted all-predecessor response rows see only which retained worlds currently share a complete input tuple. The binary selector lower bound shows that no uniformly coarser exact state exists under the declared causal residual interface.
project_justification.fill: The project keeps the standard parent-subset SCM class as its target, invokes the sourced canonical-carrier equivalence, proves deterministic normalization and equality-type continuation on that carrier, derives complete representative transitions and explicit \(h\)- and \(r\)-dependent bounds, reconstructs sparse response systems, certifies sharp endpoints for the standard class, and proves \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) by a pin-resistant binary construction. The lower bound concerns exact continuation states, not running time or all decision-diagram representations.

body.related_work: Rossetto and Antonucci, in \emph{Partial Identification under Causal Orders by Linear Programming}, establish in Theorems~1--4 and their lifted-program and constructive-sharpness results the exact order-only identified set and the equivalence that permits optimization over complete all-predecessor response signatures even when a standard recursive model has parent subsets. The present compiler takes that sourced equivalence as its interface and tightens the query-specific construction for small \(h\); it does not redefine arbitrary recursive structural causal models as saturated. Halpern supplies finite recursive causal certificates and broad satisfiability hardness, but not a world-count continuation parameter; predecessor-only retained contexts are derived by the normalization lemma rather than imposed as Halpern syntax or as a maintained assumption. Ganian, Gr\"{u}ndel, and Wietheger, in the 2025 preprint \emph{Gateways to Tractability for Satisfiability in Pearl's Causal Hierarchy}, study \(\mathrm{SAT}^{\mathrm{lin}}_{\mathrm{counterfact}}\), whose inputs are inequalities over probability terms on one common domain, and prove fixed-parameter tractability in their \(d+n\) parameter; no reduction, embedding, separation, or tightening is claimed here. Huber and coauthors, in \emph{Tractable Bounding of Counterfactual Queries by Knowledge Compilation}, compile fixed structural equations into arithmetic circuits for approximate causal-EM inner bounds; the present problem instead exactly quantifies, through the causal-order canonical carrier, over the standard parent-subset models compatible with \(p\) alone. Darwiche and Marquis supply the general distinction between succinctness and supported online operations, but no causal residual theorem; the present binary selector construction proves the Bell-state lower bound directly. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim cover arbitrary graphs and heterogeneous data through canonical polynomial programs, a broader setting excluded here. Han, Chen, and Darwiche control multi-world width when mechanisms are fully specified, whereas the current state quantifies over unknown mechanisms. Zaffalon and coauthors demonstrate the hardness of partially specified graphical models even on polytrees, explaining why prescribed sparse graphs are not absorbed into the order-only result.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The equality partition is insufficient when a sparse parent graph is prescribed as part of the model class. In the chain \(A\to B\to Y\) without \(A\to Y\), two two-world histories can have the same partition of complete \((A,B)\) prefixes but different equality of the actual parent \(B\) supplied to \(Y\), hence different feasible future outcomes. The standard order-compatible target class allows parent subsets, but its sharp-bound optimization uses the Rossetto--Antonucci saturated canonical carrier; that equivalence does not license the same quotient after conditioning on a prescribed sparse graph. The Bell-state lower bound is correspondingly scoped to the declared saturated-carrier residual interface and does not imply an \(h\log h\) time lower bound or a lower bound for all reduced multi-valued decision diagrams. Dense input reading, explicit unnesting, and rational bit complexity are charged; prescribed sparse graphs, independence restrictions, cycles, succinct nested syntax, and experimental-table constraints are excluded.
body.honest_scope: The Rossetto--Antonucci canonical equivalence from standard order-compatible parent-subset models to the saturated all-predecessor response carrier is credited and restated only as an interface proposition. The normalization lemma, continuation theorem, representative bounds, joint truth-state compiler, sparse reconstruction, cellwise attainment, false-bit criterion, and self-contained numeric-history separation are proved within that interface. The residual result now proves the exact characterization \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) using \(h\) nonfactual retained contexts and a separate factual zero cell; it makes no \(h\log h\) time-lower-bound claim and no claim about all reduced decision diagrams. Sanity Corollary~1 records the factual reduction and credits its \(r=1\) endpoint equality to Rossetto--Antonucci without a novelty claim. The standard finite-model certificate, broad hardness, completed-response sharpness, and sample-mean inference are credited rather than claimed. Prescribed-sparse-graph, factorized-exogenous, multi-regime, and direct nested-syntax extensions remain outside scope.
body.interpretation: The equality partition forgets all numeric prefix labels and retains exactly the cross-world coincidence information that an unrestricted next response row can observe. The lower-bound family shows that every one of the \(\operatorname{Bell}(h)\) coincidence patterns can matter to a later causal conjunction, even with binary variables and factual zeros. This is optimality for the declared exact online residual state; it neither lower-bounds total running time nor rules out compression tailored to a fixed query or a different compilation language.
